title: I Carried a Baby for My Brother, but the Moment He Saw His Newborn Daughter, He Refused to Take Her Home
fb_text:
I carried a baby for my brother, but the moment he saw his newborn daughter, he turned her away. And the reason he gave horrified me. 😰😨

My brother and his wife had been trying to have a child for years. When they finally asked me to be their surrogate, I said yes.

My brother had always been the closest person to me, and my best friend. He had supported me and stood by me through every hard time. I already had a son, and I understood the kind of love they dreamed of knowing. I wanted to help them.

Most of all, whenever I saw my brother spending time with my son, he seemed happier than ever.

When they learned it would be a girl, they started buying tiny dresses and toys. They even painted the nursery pink. Every time they visited, they talked about nothing else.

When I finally gave birth, they came to the hospital right away.

His wife burst into tears of joy the first time she saw her baby.

Then my brother took the baby in his arms.

He looked at her in silence for a few seconds.

Suddenly, his face turned deathly pale.

When I asked if everything was all right, he answered in a shaking voice:

"I'm sorry, but... I can't take her."

I thought I'd misheard. The room fell completely silent.

"She's your daughter. What are you talking about?"

He looked his wife straight in the eyes. Then he looked at me and said:

"I'm sorry, but I won't bring her home."

And he placed the baby back in my arms.

In tears, his wife demanded to know why they couldn't take their daughter home.

My brother let out a deep sigh. His face had turned red, and he said:

"Look at her back. We can't do this. She can't be our daughter."

My heart was pounding as I looked at the baby's back, and I nearly fainted.

His wife screamed so loudly that the whole floor heard her. Hospital staff rushed in at once to find out what had happened.

article_html:
My brother and his wife had been trying to have a child for years. Every test, every treatment and every disappointment had worn them down, and I had watched it all happen. So when they finally sat me down and asked if I would be their surrogate, I did not hesitate. I said yes.

My brother had always been the closest person in the world to me, and my best friend. He had supported me and stood by me through every hard time in my life. I already had a son of my own, so I understood the kind of love they were dreaming of knowing. I wanted to give it to them.

Most of all, whenever I saw my brother spending time with my son, he seemed happier than ever. He was born to be a father. I was sure of it.

A Nursery Painted Pink

When they learned it would be a girl, they started buying tiny dresses and soft toys. They painted the nursery pink and talked about names. Every visit, they showed me something new they had found for her. Carrying that little girl, I felt proud, and I felt close to them in a way I never had before.

When I finally went into labor, they rushed to the hospital and were there almost immediately.

His wife burst into tears of joy the first time she saw her baby. She laughed and cried at the same time, and I felt that every difficult month had been worth it.

The Moment Everything Changed

Then my brother took the baby in his arms.

He looked at her in silence for a few seconds. Suddenly, his face turned deathly pale.

I asked him if everything was all right. In a shaking voice, he answered, "I'm sorry, but... I can't take her."

I thought I had misheard. "She's your daughter," I said. "What are you talking about?"

He looked his wife straight in the eyes. Then he looked at me and said, "I'm sorry, but I won't bring her home."

And he placed the baby back in my arms.

In tears, his wife demanded to know why they couldn't take their daughter home. My brother let out a deep sigh. His face had turned red.

"Look at her back," he said. "We can't do this. She can't be our daughter."

I turned the baby gently and looked. Across her tiny back was a large, dark mark, with an irregular shape, nothing like the smooth skin I had expected. For a moment my head spun and I nearly fainted. I did not know what it was, and my first thought was that something terrible was wrong with her.

His wife screamed so loudly that the whole floor heard her. Hospital staff rushed in to find out what had happened.

What the Doctor Said

A pediatrician arrived within minutes. She examined the baby carefully while the room stayed frozen, and then she spoke in a calm, steady voice.

"This is a birthmark," she said. "It's quite large, but it's completely harmless. Your daughter is healthy. It will not hurt her, and it does not mean anything is wrong."

My brother shook his head. He said that neither of them had a mark like that, and that he was afraid there had been some terrible mistake. He was afraid the child was not theirs.

That was the part that horrified me. It was not the mark. It was the fact that, in the first minute of her life, he had been ready to turn his back on his own daughter because of how she looked.

"You are saying this about a baby who is less than an hour old," I told him. My voice was shaking. "She has done nothing except be born."

His wife stood up. She wiped her face and held out her arms for her daughter. "I have waited for her for years," she said quietly. "I am not leaving without her. And you can decide right now whether you are coming with us."

A Father Finds His Way

The doctor offered a test to put his fears to rest, and he agreed. The result was exactly what his wife and I had known all along. The baby was theirs, with no mistake and no mix-up.

When the nurse told him, my brother sat down on the edge of the chair and covered his face with his hands. For a long time he said nothing. Then he told us he had panicked. He had imagined that people would stare, that she would be teased, that he would not know how to protect her. Fear had spoken for him before love had a chance to.

He asked his wife to forgive him. He asked me to forgive him too. Then, with trembling hands, he asked if he could hold his daughter again.

I placed her in his arms. This time he did not look away. He touched her small hand, and the tears finally came. "I'm so sorry," he whispered to her. "I'm here. I'm your dad."

It was not easy for his wife to forget what had happened, and I will not pretend it was. They spent a lot of time talking in the weeks that followed, and I think they both needed it. But he never again let go of that little girl in any way that mattered. He was the first to wake for her at night, and the first to say she was beautiful.

Today, when I see my brother with his daughter, I remember how close we came to losing that moment. I am glad I carried her. And I am glad he was brave enough to see her for what she truly was, his child, exactly as she came into the world.

source.text:
J’ai été mère porteuse pour mon frère, mais lorsqu’il a vu sa fille nouveau-née, il l’a rejetée. Et la raison pour laquelle il a fait cela m’a horrifiée. 😰😨

Mon frère et sa femme essayaient d’avoir un enfant depuis des années. Lorsqu’ils m’ont finalement demandé d’être leur mère porteuse, j’ai accepté.

Mon frère avait toujours été la personne la plus proche de moi et mon meilleur ami. Il m’avait toujours soutenue et avait toujours été là pour moi dans les moments difficiles. J’avais déjà un fils et je comprenais le genre d’amour qu’ils rêvaient de connaître. Je voulais les aider.

Surtout, chaque fois que je voyais mon frère passer du temps avec mon fils, il semblait plus heureux que jamais.

Lorsqu’ils ont appris que ce serait une fille, ils ont commencé à acheter de petites robes et des jouets. Ils ont même peint la chambre du bébé en rose.

Lorsque j’ai enfin accouché, ils sont immédiatement venus à l’hôpital.

La femme a fondu en larmes de joie lorsqu’elle a vu son bébé pour la première fois.

Puis mon frère a pris le bébé dans ses bras.

Il l’a regardée en silence pendant quelques secondes.

Soudain, son visage est devenu livide.

Lorsque je lui ai demandé si tout allait bien, il m’a répondu d’une voix tremblante :

— Je suis désolé, mais… je ne peux pas la prendre.

J’ai cru avoir mal entendu.

— C’est ta fille. Qu’est-ce que tu racontes ?

Il a regardé sa femme droit dans les yeux.

Puis il m’a regardée et m’a dit :

— Je suis désolé, mais je ne la ramènerai pas à la maison.

Et il a remis le bébé dans mes bras.

En larmes, sa femme a exigé de savoir pourquoi ils ne pouvaient pas ramener leur fille chez eux.

Mon frère a poussé un profond soupir. Son visage était devenu rouge, puis il a dit :

— Regarde son dos. On ne peut pas faire ça. Elle ne peut pas être notre fille.

J’ai regardé le dos du bébé et j’ai failli m’évanouir.

Sa femme a crié si fort que tout l’étage l’a entendue. Le personnel de l’hôpital s’est immédiatement précipité pour comprendre ce qui s’était passé.
